title: The Lane That Carried 1,800 veh/h, Not 1,227
featured_title: THE LANE THAT CARRIED 1800 VEHICLES PER HOUR NOT 1227
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The spacing was 132 ft per vehicle, but 45 mph was treated as 45 ft/s. Correct unit conversion gives density 40 veh/mi and flow 1,800 veh/h/lane.

practice.primary_question: How are average space headway, traffic density, speed, and flow related for a uniform traffic stream?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Combining miles per hour with feet of spacing without converting the distance units.

case_dna.target_misconception: A speed stated as 45 mph can be used numerically as 45 ft/s when computing time headway from spacing in feet.
case_dna.why_plausible: Both are speed units, and the numerical value can be carried into a headway equation if units are ignored.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: At 45 mph, speed is 66 ft/s. With 132 ft/veh spacing, time headway is 2.0 s/veh and flow is 1,800 veh/h/lane. Equivalently, density=40 veh/mi and q=kv=1,800.
case_dna.corrected_model: Use consistent units or convert spacing to density in veh/mi before applying q=kv.

problem_statement: A uniform traffic stream has average space headway of 132 ft/vehicle and average speed of 45 mph on one lane. A note treats 45 mph as 45 ft/s, calculates a 2.93 s headway, and reports about 1,227 veh/h. Determine the correct density, time headway, and lane flow.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The traffic equation was fine. The speed units were not.

options.label: Convert density to veh/mi and use q=kv
options.reason: This keeps miles and hours consistent.

options.label: Use 45/132 directly
options.reason: The speed and spacing use incompatible distance units.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the flow
gates.hint: Convert 132 ft/veh into vehicles per mile.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The density-speed relation closes the traffic stream

cards.text: 45 mph=66 ft/s, so time headway=132/66=2.0 s/veh.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the traffic-flow note
report: C3. Using 45 ft/s gives h=2.93 s and q≈1,227 veh/h.

correction.template: k={density} veh/mi/lane, h={headway_s} s, q={flow} veh/h/lane.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Limit flow to 1,500 veh/h at 45 mph
gates.constraint: Assume speed remains 45 mph and uniform spacing.

options.label: Increase average spacing to at least 158.4 ft/veh

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply q=kv again
gates.prompt: Average spacing is 176 ft/veh and speed is 60 mph. What is flow?

options.label: About 1,364 veh/h/lane
options.reason: That comes from mixing incompatible units.

gates.explanation: Traffic flow equals density times speed when units are consistent.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the traffic-flow calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that speed, spacing, density, and flow must be expressed in consistent units before using traffic-flow equations.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Miles per hour was treated as feet per second.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The required unit conversion between miles and feet.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use consistent units and q=kv, or compute time headway with speed in ft/s.

seo.seo_title: Traffic Flow Density and Speed | FE Civil E-105
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil E-105: 132 ft/vehicle spacing at 45 mph gives 40 veh/mi/lane and 1,800 veh/h/lane, not 1,227.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil traffic flow density speed
seo.excerpt: Traffic-flow equations fail quickly when miles per hour are mixed with feet of spacing.
seo.direct_answer: k=5280/132=40 veh/mi/lane. Therefore q=kv=40×45=1800 veh/h/lane. The equivalent time headway is 2.0 s/veh.

faqs.q: What is the fundamental traffic-flow relation?
faqs.a: q=kv, where flow equals density times speed with consistent units.
